messages:
Evelyn (CSE): ACME pinged — after last night's fp8-calib rollout their endpoint p95 jumped ~30% and some 500s. They attached traces.
Bob (ACME Support): Confirmed. Deployed v2.7.3-calib-fp8 at 02:12. Observed latency and occasional worker 500s. Rolling back to fp16 brought p95 to normal. Logs: 
``nchosen_kernel: int4_conv_kv
kernel_fallback: fp16_matmul_slow_path
kvc_churn=20/min
error=500 worker_timeout
```
Evelyn: Can eng look? Customer wants root cause and mitigation plan. @mike?
Mike (eng-runtime): I'll take it. Need full GPU trace (nvtx/nvprof), kernel roster metadata from the calibration snapshot, and a sample of their seq length distribution.
Bob (ACME Support): Uploading traces now. Typical seq_len 45-80, mostly batch_size=1.
Nora (eng-ml): Odd that chosen_kernel shows int4_conv_kv for an fp8-calib variant; calibration must have altered kernel candidate weights. If calibration used long-seq data it can bias toward throughput kernels.
Alejandro (oncall): Pulling timeline: repeated KV reloads cause cache-state flips. Each flip triggers kernel selection logic which sometimes picks a throughput-optimized kernel that has higher token startup cost, hurting p95 for small-batch traffic.
Mike (eng-runtime): Our selector currently ranks kernels by a score vector produced at calibration time. If the score favors throughput_kernel and we have cache_evictions, the amortized cost is worse for short sequences.
Evelyn: Short-term mitigations?
Mike (eng-runtime): Options:
- Keep ACME on fp16 (they already rolled back)
- Apply a per-route kernel whitelist to stop selector from choosing the suspect throughput kernels (config-only)
- Increase tenant KV cache quota to reduce churn
- Temporarily disable the new calibration snapshot for this model
I'll push a whitelist override if ACME wants immediate relief.
Bob (ACME Support): Please do. They want minimal disruption but need p95 stable.
Lina (eng-platform): We can push a config flag scoped to the route; no restart. I can apply it and monitor.
Alejandro (oncall): Starting a repro run on our dedicated canary cluster with seq_dist 48-72, batch_size=1, and forced cache-eviction events to match their telemetry. Early microbench shows ~27% p95 regression when kvc_churn > 12/min on the fp8-calib snapshot.
Snippet from tracer:
``
if (kvc_churn > 12) {
  preferred = throughput_kernel;
} else {
  preferred = low_latency_kernel;
}
```
Mike (eng-runtime): That's the current heuristic. Fix: only promote throughput_kernel when median_seq_len > 128 OR batch_size > 4 OR sustained throughput mode detected. I'll open a PR to guard promotion with sequence/batch thresholds.
Nora (eng-ml): I'll run calibration audit comparing activation histograms and sequence-length sampling used for calibration vs production traffic. If we find skew, regenerate calibration with a representative sample or add p95 latency as a penalty term in the calibration objective.
Evelyn: What's ETA for whitelist and the selector guard?
Mike (eng-runtime): Whitelist via platform config -> ~15-30m. Selector guard PR -> ~2h to land, canary ~4-6h, prod ~24h after canary. Increasing KV cache quota -> immediate config change if ACME approves slight resource bump.
Bob (ACME Support): Whitelist applied. ACME telemetry: p95 returned to baseline within ~3 minutes. They're asking for an RCA note and a timeline for when fp8-calib can safely be re-enabled.
Sam (PM): Draft comms: apology + immediate rollback restored performance, temporary whitelist applied, root cause: calibration snapshot biased kernel ordering that interacted poorly with tenant KV churn; planned fixes & timeline; offer a validation run using ACME workload before re-enabling. Keep it concise and engineering-transparent.
Nora (eng-ml): Long-term: add latency-aware constraints to calibration and keep a fallback calibration snapshot for instant rollback when new calibration changes candidate ordering. Also add a telemetry diff that alerts when calibration changes the top-N kernel ranking for an active route.
Alejandro (oncall): Created INF-4829; attached nvprof timelines, kernel roster diffs, and microbench traces. Repro artifacts show exact kernel_switch sequence around cache rehydrate events.
Mike (eng-runtime): Action items: whitelist pushed (done), PR for selector guard opened, add alert for calibration-induced kernel reordering.
Lina (eng-platform): Monitoring dashboards updated for ACME route; will send alert if p95 deviates during canary.
Evelyn: I'll send the customer update and schedule a joint postmortem with eng-runtime and eng-ml. Include before/after p95 graphs.
Bob (ACME Support): Customer accepted the explanation and prefers we only re-enable fp8-calib after canary + validated run under their seq/batch distribution.
Evelyn: Thanks team. Keep thread updated.
Bob (ACME Support): Thanks all :thumbsup:
